name: WeChat LocalMind
description: Zero-dependency on macOS, strictly read-only full-account local WeChat 3.x and 4.x (WCDB) chat extractor (1-on-1 DMs, groups, official accounts), structured cleaner, CLI, and JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP Stdio Server for AI Agents. Decrypts SQLCipher 3/4 shards and .db-wal logs into an incremental offline snapshot, enforces configurable chat_scope and allow/block policies, auto-decodes 3.x XOR and 4.x V1/V2 .dat images, and makes zero outbound network calls.
applicationSubCategory: Local-first Chat Data Extractor & MCP Server
featureList: Full-account local WeChat chat extraction covering 1-on-1 DMs (wxid_*, custom aliases, @openim, filehelper), group chats (@chatroom, @im.chatroom), and official accounts (gh_*, notifymessage, weixin)
SQLCipher 3 (reserve=48) and SQLCipher 4 / WeChat 4.x WCDB (reserve=80) offline decryption with .db-wal frame replay using macOS CommonCrypto or cryptography/PyCryptodome
WeChat 4.x zstd in-memory decompression via Python 3.14 compression.zstd, libzstd.dylib, or zstd CLI
Persistent incremental snapshot watermarks across message_0.db..message_N.db and MSG*.db with globally monotonic msg_id cursors and FTS5 trigram search
Configurable chat_scope (all, groups, direct, official) and blacklist/whitelist policy enforcement (EXIT_POLICY_DENIED = 3)
4-tier real-name resolution (remark > group_nickname > nick_name > anonymized wxid/gh/contact ID) and @wxid_ mention normalization

XML and Protobuf wire parsing for 150-character <refermsg> quote chains, <recorditem> merged forwards, <voicetrans> transcripts, rich appmsg subtypes, revoked message stripping, and reversible ack folding
Adaptive magic-header XOR and WeChat 4.x V1/V2 AES-128-ECB+XOR decryption for WeChat .dat images into .jpg, .png, .gif, .webp, .bmp, and .heic
12 CLI subcommands (with list-chats and list-groups aliases), 5 read-only JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP Stdio tools (readOnlyHint: true), and SKILL.md agent bundle
softwareRequirements: Zero third-party pip packages on macOS (uses built-in CommonCrypto and stdlib)
Optional cryptography or PyCryptodome on Linux/non-macOS for AES backends
